newsitem.title: USA: Phillips, Corpoven eye Texas refinery upgrade.
newsitem.headline: Phillips, Corpoven eye Texas refinery upgrade.

text.p: State-owned Petroleos de Venezuela unit Corpoven is conducting a joint study with Phillips to determine the feasibility of upgrading the U.S. company's Sweeny, Texas, refinery, a PDVSA source said Thursday.
The study is part of Corpoven's negotiations with Phillips to buy a 50 percent stake in the refinery.
Asked how the talks are progressing, the source said, "First we have to finish the study to see if the refinery can take heavy crude. With small changes, the refinery could take heavy crude."
Most of Venezuela's crude is heavy and sour. Caracas has been looking to secure more strategic outlets in the United States for its growing production.
The joint study should be completed in a "few months" the source said.
The Sweeny refinery has a capacity of around 200,000 barrels per day, and now processes a variety of crudes, a refinery spokesman said.

A Phillips spokesman declined to comment on the specific negotiations. "We are looking for creative ways to improve the profitability of our refining, marketing and transportation operations, including joint ventures," a spokesman at the company's headquarters said.
